title: Grateful Dead Live at Ohio Theatre on 1971-10-31
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v7.02 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of an energetic 1971 show featuring a smoking Dark Star and standout El Paso, with crisp Keith piano despite minor mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers clear instrument separation and a crisp Keith Godchaux piano, making the first set a pleasure to hear even though a few mix anomalies (Keith too forward early on, occasional channel swaps) are noted. Musically the night is a highlight of the fall‑71 era – Dark Star soars, El Paso shines, and Jack Straw grooves, with the audience feeding the band’s high energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently glowing reviews (12 total) praise both performance (standout Dark Star, El Paso, overall energy) and recording quality (crisp piano, good separation), with only minor mix complaints, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp Keith piano and solid instrument separation; occasional mix issues such as Keith being overly high in the early Bertha and unexpected left/right channel swaps for Bobby and Jerry.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical fall ’71 first‑set flow with brisk pacing; a few deliberately slower renditions (e.g., Casey Jones) add variety but the overall momentum stays high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s improvisational riffs are highlighted, especially in Dark Star and El Paso, earning praise for inventive solos.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass provides a tight foundation and he joins the vocal harmonies on Jack Straw, noted as solid and supportive.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s piano is crisp and present throughout, though the mix makes it too forward early in the set before being corrected later.
